subject: Post-call: token budget, streaming behavior & SLO action items (Acme AI)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sam Woods <sam.woods@acmeai.com>, eng@acmeai.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: token budget, streaming behavior & SLO action items (Acme AI)

Hi Sam / Acme team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned on perf expectations and what we need to validate on our side.

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Product SLO: interactive assistant with p95 end-to-end response latency <= 300ms for typical queries (measured end-to-end; first-token streaming + time to finish streaming considered).
- Typical payload: combined context ~5,000–6,000 input tokens (user history + retrieved docs), expected generation up to 800–1,200 output tokens in longer cases.
- Concurrency target: 120 concurrent active users for the initial pilot, scaling to 400 over 12 months.
- Streaming: client expects first-token within ~200ms and progressive updates (chunked stream, 64-token chunks preferred).
- Availability: fall back to a lower-cost model if spikes occur; fallbacks must preserve coherent responses for short contexts.

Initial observations from our side (high level):
- With an 8k model variant and no batching, a 6k input + 1k output runs materially into tail latency due to attention costs and KV cache size. First-token latency can be significantly improved with prefix/KV reuse and streaming optimizations; tail depends on output token count and chunking.
- For SLOs in the ~300ms p95 band we’ll need: a) a dedicated serving pool (predictable GPU), b) tuned streaming chunk sizes (we suggest starting at 64 tokens), and c) workload-aware caching for repeated context fragments.

What we need from Acme to run targeted qualification:
1) Sample payloads (JSONL) representative of 80th/95th percentile queries (include average and peak-length contexts).
2) Clarify how you measure p95 today (first-byte vs last-byte).
3) Estimate percent of requests that truly need 1k+ output tokens vs those that are short (<= 256 tokens).

Proposed immediate next steps (timeline):
- Today: Acme shares sample payloads (see items above).
- 48–72h: Redwood run micro-bench (single-client) to estimate first-token vs full-response latencies across model variants and chunk sizes. Attachments will include our quick bench notes.
- 1 week: Redwood produce a short SLO runbook with recommended Dedicated pool sizing, fallback model candidates, and a canary config for a 2-week pilot.

I attached a bench-summary-quicknotes.txt with our initial ballpark numbers, and a draft canary config we’ll refine after the sample payloads.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internal owners once we have the sample data.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sam Woods <sam.woods@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: token budget, streaming behavior & SLO action items (Acme AI)

Thanks Evelyn — a few notes from perf side and what I’ll run with once we have payloads: 

Bench notes (ballpark from local runs on A100/80GB equivalent):
- Model family: 8k and 16k-context variants we discussed show these patterns:
  - 4k input + 256 output: first-token ~120–160ms, full-response ~220–300ms (single request).
  - 6k input + 1k output: first-token ~210–260ms, full-response p95 ~480–700ms depending on chunk size and generator tuning.
- Streaming chunking matters: 32-token chunks reduce perceived latency for short answers but increase per-chunk overhead; 64-token chunk is a pragmatic starting point to balance first-byte latency and throughput.

Open questions for Acme (please confirm):
- Is your p95 requirement tied to user-visible completion (last-byte) or first-token arrival? We need to instrument the right telemetry.
- Do you expect many concurrent long-run generations (1k+ tokens) or are those rare exceptions? That drives how much tail capacity we reserve.

When I get the sample payloads I’ll run: single-request latency matrix (models x chunk-size x concurrency 1), then a small concurrency sweep (1, 10, 50, 120) to estimate queuing and batching effects. I’ll attach a short CSV with the numbers.

Ben
Ben Carter
Perf Eng, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Woods <sam.woods@acmeai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@acmeai.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: token budget, streaming behavior & SLO action items (Acme AI)

Hi Evelyn/Ben — attaching the sample payloads (acme_sample_payloads_20270214.jsonl). The file contains:
- 500 representative requests: labels for 50th/80th/95th percentiles by context size.
- Fields: user_history_tokens, doc_tokens, expected_output_target_tokens, client_chunk_pref.

Answers inline to your questions:
- p95 measurement: user-visible completion (last-byte) is how our product teams define the SLO, but first-token timing is also important for UX. We expect both to be part of the contract (first-byte target ~200ms, last-byte target ~300ms p95).
- Output length distribution: ~78% of requests expect <=256 tokens; ~18% expect 256–800; ~4% could be >800 (rare).
- We can also expose a flag in the sample set to mark requests that must finish strictly coherently (no model fallback). Roughly 25% require strict model fidelity.

We’re OK doing an initial pilot on Dedicated with a canary; we’d like Redwood’s recommendation for pool sizing and an explicit fallback model list (low-cost for spike scenarios).

Thanks — Sam
Sam Woods
Lead Product Manager, Acme AI

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sam Woods <sam.woods@acmeai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: token budget, streaming behavior & SLO action items (Acme AI)

Perfect — thanks for the payloads and the distribution breakdown, that’s exactly what we need. Action list and owners below: 

Action items (owners / ETA):
1) Run baseline micro-bench (single-client) matrix across candidate models and chunk sizes (Ben) — ETA 48 hours. Output: CSV with first-token and full-response p50/p95. Attachment: bench-summary-quicknotes.txt
2) Run small concurrency sweep (Ben + infra) to estimate queuing/batching at 1, 10, 50, 120 concurrent sessions — ETA 72 hours.
3) Draft canary config and Dedicated pool sizing recommendation (Marissa) — ETA 5 business days. Will include fallback model list and autoscale thresholds.
4) Define telemetry instrumentation spec (Evelyn) so Acme and Redwood measure the same p95s (first-byte vs last-byte). I’ll share a short doc by tomorrow EOD.
5) Agreement on strict-fidelity subset and fallback semantics (Sam + Redwood) — discuss in follow-up call.

Proposed follow-up: 2027-02-17T10:00 PST — 30m call to review bench results and canary. Please confirm.

I’m going to create a short Jira (PIPE-907) to track these tasks and link the artifacts.

Thanks all — eager to get the numbers and a recommended pilot plan.

Best,
Evelyn

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sam Woods <sam.woods@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: token budget, streaming behavior & SLO action items (Acme AI)

Ack — I’ll draft the canary and pool-sizing recommendation. Preliminary notes:
- Canary: 2-week run on Dedicated with a 4-GPU pool sized to handle 120 concurrent sessions with conservative headroom (reserve for 20% burst).
- Fallbacks: recommend a 4k-context cheaper variant and a quantized 8k variant; classify requests flagged as "strict-fidelity" to never fallback.
- Autoscale triggers: scale up if 95th CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 1m and average queue latency > 50ms.

I’ll share a YAML draft (redwood_canary_config_draft.yaml) by end of day tomorrow.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success / Solutions, Redwood Inference
